patients.summary: Construction foreman in his early thirties who joined the practice in August 2025 with intermittent low back pain and pollen allergies. A car crash in November 2025 left an incomplete anterior cord injury over a T8 wedge fracture, from which he recovered to walking with a cane; in June 2026, as a motorcycle passenger, he sustained a complete T4 cord injury with neurogenic shock and is in inpatient rehab at today.

documents.body: Caller is a 32 y/o man looking for a new PCP; his last doctor retired and the office closed. Commercial PPO card info taken. Works as a construction foreman, prefers early morning appointments before job site. New patient visit set for Wed 8/20 at 7:30. Records release signed electronically, request sent to his prior primary care office. Reminded to bring his medications or a list.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
32 y/o M establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

Concerns today: none acute. Wants a doctor he can text when his back acts up.

Back: on and off low back ache for about four years, mechanical, worse after a long day lifting or bending on site, better with rest. Never radiates, no numbness or weakness, no bladder or bowel trouble. Takes ibuprofen 400 mg a few times a month when it flares. Never had imaging.

Allergies (nose): spring and again late summer, sneezing and runny nose. Loratadine 10 mg on the bad days works fine.

PMH: as above.
PSH: arthroscopic knee surgery at 28, recovered without issues.
Meds: ibuprofen 400 mg PRN back pain; loratadine 10 mg daily PRN.
Allergies: penicillin - hives as a kid.
FHx: father with high blood pressure. Mother hypothyroid. One brother, healthy.
SHx: single, lives on his own in Sunderland. Construction foreman. Former smoker, about 5 pack-years, quit 2 years ago and has stayed off. Alcohol 2-3 drinks a week, socially. No drug use.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI around 26-27. Well appearing. HEENT unremarkable, nasal mucosa pink. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear throughout. Abdomen soft, nontender. Back: no midline tenderness, full flexion with mild tightness at end range, straight leg raise negative both sides. Knees without effusion. Neuro: strength 5/5 in the legs, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, sensation intact. Skin clear. PHQ-9 = 2.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Intermittent mechanical low back pain - no red flags. Ibuprofen PRN with food, core and hip strengthening handout, lifting mechanics. PT if flares become frequent.
2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis - loratadine PRN, fine to continue.
3. Health maintenance - Tdap today (no record of last one). CBC, CMP, lipids. One-time hep C and HIV screening, he agreed. Flu and COVID when the fall supply arrives.
4. Former smoker - congratulated, nothing further needed at his age and exposure.

RTC yearly physical, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Cameron - all of your bloodwork from Wednesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests are normal, and the hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. LDL cholesterol is a touch above the lab's range at 116; at 32 with no other risk factors that is not something to treat, just worth rechecking in a few years. Nothing to change. Good to have you with us. Reach out anytime the back flares up.

Records received from patient's former primary care office (closed; records custodian sent summary). Covers visits 2018-2024.

Surgical: arthroscopic knee procedure (side not documented in summary), outside orthopedics, uneventful recovery.
Medications: ibuprofen 400 mg as needed; loratadine 10 mg as needed.

Smoking: current smoker in 2018-2022 notes, recorded as quit in 2023.
Routine physicals with normal exams and normal blood pressures. No imaging of the spine on file.

Reviewed by PCP, consistent with intake history. Filed.

documents.title: Immunization visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In before work for fall vaccines. Feeling well, no fever. Penicillin allergy noted, no vaccine reactions in the past. Influenza 0.5 mL IM left deltoid; COVID updated formula 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. Lots and VIS documented. Waited 15 minutes, left in good shape for his shift.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department
ED visit 11/04/2025, received by the practice 11/06/2025

CC: back pain, can't move legs.

HPI: 32-year-old man brought in by EMS after a car crash; he took a direct hit to the back. Reports severe back pain and says he cannot move his legs since the collision. Baseline history of intermittent mechanical low back pain and seasonal allergic rhinitis.

PMH: intermittent mechanical low back pain; seasonal allergic rhinitis.
PSH: knee arthroscopy at 28.
Home meds: ibuprofen 400 mg PRN back pain, loratadine 10 mg daily PRN.
Allergies: PENICILLIN (hives).
FHx: father HTN, mother hypothyroidism, brother healthy.
SHx: former smoker (5 pack-years, quit 2 yrs). Social alcohol 2-3/week. Construction foreman.

Vitals: BP 130/85, HR 88, RR 18.

Exam: Alert, in obvious pain. Spinal precautions maintained. Both lower extremities flaccid with no voluntary movement; patellar and Achilles-level deep tendon reflexes absent bilaterally. Pain and temperature sensation lost from the T10 dermatome downward. Joint position and vibration sense preserved in both legs. Upper extremities with normal strength. Abdomen soft.

Imaging: MRI of the spine - anterior wedge compression fracture of the T8 vertebral body; swelling with abnormal signal involving the anterior portion of the spinal cord at that level.

Impression: anterior cord syndrome secondary to T8 anterior wedge compression fracture after MVC.

Disposition: spine surgery and trauma consulted; admitted to the trauma service.

events.reason: Anterior cord syndrome with T8 compression fracture

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - transfer to inpatient rehabilitation
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, trauma service
Admitted 11/04/2025 - Discharged 11/11/2025 to acute inpatient rehabilitation

Principal diagnosis: anterior cord syndrome, thoracic, from T8 anterior wedge compression fracture (motor vehicle collision).

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED. Seen by spine surgery; fracture managed without surgery in a custom TLSO for all upright activity. Mean arterial pressure was kept above 85 for the first several days per spinal cord injury protocol, in the step-down unit. Enoxaparin started for DVT prophylaxis once cleared by spine. Pain controlled. Voiding on his own after catheter removal; bowels moving.

Neuro at transfer: trace hip flexion now present on both sides; otherwise legs remain weak. Sensory loss to pin and temperature below T10 unchanged; proprioception and vibration intact.

Allergies: penicillin (hives).

Medications at transfer: enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously daily (prophylaxis); loratadine 10 mg daily PRN; ibuprofen 400 mg PRN (home).

Follow-up: transferring to inpatient rehab. Spine clinic / PM&R to follow brace and imaging. PCP copied.

documents.title: Call from patient's brother
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Brother called. Cameron was in a car accident last night, admitted to the regional hospital with a spine injury and can't move his legs. Patient gave verbal permission by phone in the background for us to speak with brother. Brother asks that we stay in the loop. Told him we'd request records and that the hospital team should call us at discharge. Routed to PCP.

PCP addendum: Will follow. Please flag the ED record and discharge summary when they arrive.

events.reason: Inpatient rehabilitation after anterior cord syndrome

documents.title: Inpatient Rehabilitation Discharge Summary
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Acute inpatient rehabilitation unit
Admitted 11/11/2025 - Discharged 12/12/2025 to home

Rehab diagnosis: incomplete thoracic spinal cord injury (anterior cord syndrome) after T8 anterior wedge compression fracture, nonoperative in TLSO.

Course: Daily PT and OT. Steady motor return in both legs over the stay. Transfers independent by week 3. Bladder and bowel continent throughout. Mood good, engaged in therapy.

Function at discharge: ambulates about 150 feet with a rolling walker and standby assist; wheelchair for longer distances and the community. Independent with dressing using adaptive equipment. TLSO whenever upright, may remove lying flat.

Sensory: pin and temperature still reduced below T10; proprioception and vibration intact.

Medications: enoxaparin discontinued at discharge now that he is walking. Home medications unchanged - ibuprofen 400 mg PRN, loratadine 10 mg daily PRN.
Allergies: penicillin (hives).

Follow-up: outpatient PT three times weekly, referral sent. Outpatient PM&R in about 8 weeks with standing thoracic x-ray. PCP visit within 2 weeks.
Equipment: rolling walker, standard wheelchair, shower chair.

documents.title: Post-discharge follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called patient 2 business days after rehab discharge. Home since Friday, brother staying with him this week. Using walker in the house, wheelchair to get to the car. Wearing brace when up. Pain manageable, using ibuprofen once a day at most. No fever, no calf pain or swelling, urinating and bowels OK. Outpatient PT starts next Monday. Reviewed med list - same as before admission, enoxaparin finished in rehab. Post-hospital visit booked Tue 12/23, ground floor room requested.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Car crash 11/4 -> T8 anterior wedge compression fracture with anterior cord syndrome. Nonoperative, TLSO. 1 week acute care, then inpatient rehab until 12/12. ED record and both discharge summaries reviewed.

Since home: walker indoors, wheelchair outside. Brother has been around most days. Outpatient PT started yesterday. Back pain at the fracture 3/10, ibuprofen 400 once a day or less. Legs feel stronger week to week. Bladder and bowel normal. No calf pain, no shortness of breath. Mood: frustrated at being off work but sleeping OK, hopeful. PHQ-9 = 4.

Meds: ibuprofen 400 mg PRN, loratadine 10 mg PRN. Enoxaparin completed in rehab.
Allergies: PCN.

Exam: vitals as charted. Arrived in wheelchair, TLSO on. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Calves soft and nontender, no leg swelling. Skin over sacrum and heels intact, no pressure areas. Legs: hip flexion and knee extension antigravity, roughly 3+/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5 both sides. Pin sensation reduced below about T10; joint position intact at the toes. Stood with walker and took several steps without loss of balance.

A/P:
1. Anterior cord syndrome, incomplete, improving - continue outpatient PT 3x/week; PM&R follow-up planned for February with standing films.
2. T8 wedge compression fracture - TLSO when upright per spine; ibuprofen PRN.
3. Post-hospital labs CBC, BMP today.
4. Low back pain, allergic rhinitis - unchanged.
5. Work - off duty; short-term disability forms completed today.

Problem list updated. RTC about 3 months, sooner as needed. Can message anytime.

documents.title: Bloodwork from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cameron, your blood count and kidney/electrolyte panel from Tuesday are normal. No anemia after the hospital stay. Keep up the PT and let me know how the February spine appointment goes.

events.reason: Follow-up after incomplete thoracic cord injury

documents.title: PM&R Outpatient Follow-up Letter
documents.author: physical medicine and rehabilitation
documents.body:
Outpatient spinal cord injury clinic
Visit date: 02/11/2026
Re: Cameron Mazur, DOB 07/01/1993

Thank you for sharing the care of Mr. Mazur, seen today about 3 months after an anterior cord syndrome from a T8 anterior wedge compression fracture (MVC 11/04/2025), managed in a TLSO.

He has done well. Now walking in the community with a single-point cane, no walker for the past few weeks. Going to outpatient PT three times a week. Mild ache at the mid back with long days on his feet. Bladder and bowel normal.

Meds: ibuprofen 400 mg PRN, loratadine 10 mg PRN. Allergy: penicillin (hives).

Exam: Gait with cane, mildly slow, no foot drop. Strength: hip flexion 4/5 and ankle dorsiflexion 4/5 on both sides; knee extension and plantarflexion near full. Pin and temperature sensation reduced below T10, unchanged; proprioception and vibration intact. No spasticity of note. Skin intact.

Standing thoracic spine x-ray, 2 views (today): T8 anterior wedge compression deformity unchanged from prior imaging, no progression of height loss or kyphosis. Alignment otherwise maintained. Other thoracic vertebral bodies normal in height.

Impression: incomplete thoracic spinal cord injury (anterior cord syndrome), good motor recovery; T8 compression fracture stable.

Plan: TLSO discontinued today. Continue outpatient PT, progress to core and endurance work. Return to clinic in 4 months. Return to construction work to be revisited at that visit; no heavy lifting until then.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up, about 4.5 months after the T8 fracture / anterior cord syndrome.

PM&R letter from 2/11 reviewed: brace off, x-ray stable, PT to continue.

Interval: walks with a cane outdoors, around the house mostly without it. PT 3x a week, working on endurance and core. The old low back ache still flares after longer PT days, same pattern as before the accident, ibuprofen 400 a couple times a week with food. No new numbness, no bowel or bladder change. Tree pollen starting, using loratadine most days. Not back at work - wants to get back to the job site, will wait for PM&R's say in June. Mood steady. PHQ-9 = 3.

Meds: ibuprofen 400 mg PRN, loratadine 10 mg daily PRN. Allergy: PCN (hives).

Exam: vitals as charted. Walks into the room with a cane, steady. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. No tenderness over the thoracic spine. Lumbar paraspinals mildly tight, no midline tenderness. Hip flexion and dorsiflexion about 4/5 both sides, rest of leg strength full. Reduced pin sensation below T10 as before.

A/P:
1. Anterior cord syndrome, incomplete, recovering well - continue PT, PM&R follow-up in June.
2. T8 compression fracture - healed/stable per PM&R.
3. Mechanical low back pain - ibuprofen PRN, limit to a few days a week, with food.
4. Seasonal allergic rhinitis - loratadine.
5. Disability paperwork - extension signed through PM&R visit.

RTC for yearly physical in August, sooner if needed.

events.reason: Motorcycle crash, unable to move legs

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department - trauma activation
ED visit 06/29/2026, received by the practice 07/02/2026

CC: motorcycle crash.

HPI: 32-year-old man, passenger on a motorcycle, thrown off and landed on his back. Arrived by EMS on a backboard. Prior history: anterior cord syndrome after a car crash in November 2025 (T8 wedge compression fracture), had recovered to walking with a cane.

PMH: anterior cord syndrome (11/2025) with T8 compression fracture; intermittent mechanical low back pain; seasonal allergic rhinitis.
PSH: knee arthroscopy at 28.
Home meds: ibuprofen 400 mg PRN, loratadine 10 mg daily PRN.
Allergies: PENICILLIN (hives).
FHx: father HTN, mother hypothyroidism, brother healthy.
SHx: former smoker (5 pack-years, quit 2 yrs). Social alcohol 2-3/week. Construction foreman.

Vitals on arrival: T 36.9 C (98.4 F), BP 84/60, HR 52.

Exam: Awake, alert, oriented. Unable to move either leg. Both legs flaccid with complete paralysis; deep tendon reflexes absent. Loss of pain, temperature, vibration and joint position sense from the level of the nipples down. Rectal: no anal tone; bulbocavernosus reflex absent. Arms with full strength and normal sensation. Foley placed, 1.1 L of retained urine drained.

Impression: acute complete thoracic spinal cord injury, sensory level T4, with neurogenic shock (hypotension with bradycardia) and spinal shock; urinary retention.

ED course: fluid resuscitation, norepinephrine started for MAP goal. CT and MRI of the spine obtained. Spine surgery and trauma at bedside. Admitted to the trauma ICU.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - transfer to inpatient rehabilitation
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, trauma service
Admitted 06/29/2026 - Discharged 07/24/2026 to acute inpatient rehabilitation

Principal diagnosis: complete spinal cord injury, upper thoracic (ASIA A, sensory level T4), from T3-T4 fracture-dislocation with cord compression, motorcycle crash.
Secondary: neurogenic shock, resolved; neurogenic bladder; neurogenic bowel. History of anterior cord syndrome with T8 compression fracture (11/2025).

Imaging: CT thoracic spine - T3-T4 fracture-dislocation. MRI thoracic spine - cord compression at T3-T4 with cord edema. The prior T8 wedge deformity is unchanged.

Procedures: 06/30/2026 posterior instrumented fusion T1-T6 with decompression (spine surgery).

Course: Trauma ICU for neurogenic shock; norepinephrine for MAP goals, weaned off by 07/03. Moved to the floor 07/05. Incision healed well. Enoxaparin DVT prophylaxis, to continue in rehab. Indwelling catheter changed to intermittent catheterization every 4-6 hours. Daily bowel program established. No pressure injuries. Seen by psychology.

Neuro at discharge: no motor or sensory function below T4, including the sacral segments (ASIA A). Arms full strength.

Allergies: penicillin (hives).
Medications at transfer: enoxaparin subcutaneously (prophylaxis); bowel program per rehab protocol; loratadine 10 mg daily PRN.

Disposition: acute inpatient rehabilitation, spinal cord injury unit. Spine surgery follow-up in 6 weeks with x-rays. PCP copied.

documents.title: Call from patient's brother
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Brother called (on file as contact from November). Cameron was hurt last night riding as a passenger on a motorcycle. In the ICU at the regional hospital, having back surgery today. Brother says the doctors told the family it is worse than last time, no feeling or movement in his legs. Offered support; told him we will request records and that he can call us anytime. Routed to PCP.

PCP addendum: Thank you. Records request sent. Will reach out to brother after surgery.
